The Commission and Department will continue to monitor prices that providers are charging and take regulatory action where required. This includes any changes in the pricing of personal care services once the service type has moved to the clinical supports contribution category from 1 October 2026. The Commission and Department appreciate the considerable and ongoing efforts of providers to implement the changes to aged care over the last few years. This level of commitment ensures older people continue to receive quality aged care services while the system undergoes major changes. Read the Minister for Aged Care and Seniors media release. Find out more about setting Support at Home prices. Read our Regulatory Bulletin on Support at Home pricing requirements and provider obligations. source_title: My Aged Care help at home and CHSP
text: Home nursing, personal care and in-home supports record: My Aged Care help at home and CHSP Category: aged_care_help_at_home Publisher: My Aged Care URL: https://www.myagedcare.gov.au/aged-care-programs/commonwealth-home-support-program Description: Entry-level help at home through My Aged Care, including personal care, nursing care, meals, domestic assistance, allied health, equipment and assessment pathways. Care team notes: Use for people generally aged 65+ or Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people aged 50+. Ask age and location before choosing My Aged Care versus NDIS.

source_title: Support at Home personal care
text: Home nursing, personal care and in-home supports record: Support at Home personal care Category: support_at_home_personal_care Publisher: My Aged Care URL: https://www.myagedcare.gov.au/news-and-updates/support-home-personal-care-contribution-changes Description: Support at Home personal care services including showering, continence support, dressing, eating, hygiene and assistance with self-administration of medication. Care team notes: Use exact dates for contribution changes. From 1 October 2026, approved personal care under Support at Home is fully government funded if assessed and funds are available.

source_title: NDIS assistance with daily life
text: Home nursing, personal care and in-home supports record: NDIS assistance with daily life Category: ndis_assistance_daily_life Publisher: NDIS URL: https://ndis.gov.au/participants/home-and-living/exploring-home-and-living-options/guide-your-ndis-home-and-living-options Description: NDIS home and living guidance on assistance with daily life, personal care, cooking, cleaning, laundry, support workers, home modifications, SIL, ILO and other home options. Care team notes: Use for people under 65 or existing NDIS participants. Separate disability-related supports from ordinary rent, groceries, bills and daily living costs.

source_title: NDIS disability-related health supports
text: Home nursing, personal care and in-home supports record: NDIS disability-related health supports Category: disability_related_health_supports Publisher: NDIS URL: https://ndis.gov.au/participants/using-your-funding/other-types-support/what-disability-related-health-support Description: NDIS guidance on disability-related health supports such as nursing or qualified therapist support, training for supporters, continence products, dressings, PEG-related food products, pressure care cushions and cough assist equipment. Care team notes: Cross-reference food/nutrition, breathing, pressure care and equipment topics. Do not treat NDIS as replacing state health responsibilities.

source_title: Support workers and personal care routines
text: Home nursing, personal care and in-home supports record: Support workers and personal care routines Category: support_workers Publisher: NDIS URL: https://ndis.gov.au/participants/working-providers/support-workers-and-recovery-coaches/what-support-worker Description: NDIS information on support workers, including household support, personal care, hygiene, dressing, medication help, registered/unregistered workers and goal-related support. Care team notes: Encourage written routines and preferences for MND care, especially transfers, communication, swallowing safety, fatigue, privacy and emergency escalation.

source_title: SIL, ILO and higher-intensity home support
text: Home nursing, personal care and in-home supports record: SIL, ILO and higher-intensity home support Category: sil_ilo_overnight_support Publisher: NDIS URL: https://ndis.gov.au/participants/home-and-living/types-home-and-living-supports/what-supported-independent-living-sil Description: NDIS information on supported independent living, individualised living options, overnight support and when higher-intensity support worker arrangements may be considered. Care team notes: MND needs can change quickly. Suggest review when overnight needs, transfers, ventilation, toileting or carer strain change.

source_title: Planned and emergency respite
text: Home nursing, personal care and in-home supports record: Planned and emergency respite Category: respite Publisher: Carer Gateway URL: https://www.carergateway.gov.au/help-and-support/caring-me/available-support-carers/planned-emergency-respite Description: Carer Gateway information on planned respite and emergency respite when a carer needs a break or cannot continue caring because of illness or injury. Care team notes: For emergency backup, link to Topic 15 emergency planning and encourage a written care plan with medicines, communication, transfers, feeding and breathing needs.

publisher: NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission / Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission
source_title: Complaints, safeguards and consumer protections
text: Home nursing, personal care and in-home supports record: Complaints, safeguards and consumer protections Category: complaints_safeguards Publisher: NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission / Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission URL: https://www.ndiscommission.gov.au/complaints/report Description: Information on raising concerns about NDIS providers/workers, aged care Support at Home protections, safety, quality, pricing transparency and complaint pathways. Care team notes: If there is harm, neglect, abuse or serious risk, advise urgent escalation through appropriate emergency/safeguarding channels and the relevant commission.

source_title: Changing in-home services as needs change
text: Home nursing, personal care and in-home supports record: Changing in-home services as needs change Category: care_plan_review Publisher: My Aged Care / NDIS URL: https://www.myagedcare.gov.au/managing-your-support-at-home-services Description: Guidance on reviewing care plans and adding/changing services when needs change, including provider discussions, reassessment pathways and budget/service-management issues. Care team notes: For MND, prompt earlier review because functional, swallowing, respiratory and carer capacity can change faster than annual review cycles.
